purpose: Plain-language handoff state for jonathanblunt1214-lgtm/Nexus-, so a different AI agent or a fresh session of the same agent can pick up work with full context. See AGENTS.md for the binding rules this file summarizes; this file is the human- and agent-readable index, not a separate source of authority.

agentCommunicationPolicy.appliesTo: Every attended progress or completion check-in message an AI agent sends to the repository owner while working on this repository.
agentCommunicationPolicy.summary: Plain language: before telling the owner about progress or that something is done, an AI must open that message with the current date and time written as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS followed by EDT or EST, e.g. 2026-08-28 08:10:42 EDT. This lets the owner tell how fresh a status update is at a glance, and lets a later session or agent reconstruct the real order of events across multiple AI agents working on this repository.

aiConflictGovernance.summary: Plain language: if two AI agents, or two runs of the same agent, make changes that could clash, the clash gets written down as an entry in AI-CONFLICTS.json instead of one side silently overwriting the other. Any conflict entry that is still open or incomplete blocks The Crucible gate, so nothing can be promoted to main while a real conflict is unresolved. Nobody force-pushes, deletes, renames, or overwrites a branch to make a conflict go away; it gets resolved and recorded instead.

crucibleGoverningDocumentInjection.afterExpiration: No external write access is granted by this exception. The Crucible or any other external system requires new explicit repository-owner authorization before writing.
crucibleGoverningDocumentInjection.summary: For this 24-hour window only, The Crucible may create, copy, inject, replace, or update files under governingDocuments/ during governance synchronization or enforcement. The permission is path-scoped and expires automatically at the stated time.

nativeGovernanceAssimilation.trigger: A Crucible-injected governingDocuments/ tree exists on Development-branch.
nativeGovernanceAssimilation.conflictPolicy: Compatible Nexus-specific rules are assimilated into the injected governing-document structure without erasing Crucible-originated requirements. Irreconcilable conflicts are recorded in AI-CONFLICTS.json and both source documents remain intact until resolved.
nativeGovernanceAssimilation.externalAuthority: Assimilation is an internal Nexus write and does not extend or renew external write access.

branchAuthoritySummary: Plain language: ordinary AI work happens only on Development-branch. An AI does not create or use claude/*, codex/*, or other auxiliary branches, and does not touch main directly, unless the repository owner explicitly authorizes that exact branch or operation in the current conversation — and that authorization does not carry over to the next task. main only changes through the protected promote-development-to-main.yml workflow. See AGENTS.md for the full, binding rules.

crucibleLearningHost.workspaceBinding: The canonical real path of the opened Nexus workspace is hashed into the project, repository, ref, and subject claims. ChatGPT project identifiers are not used.
crucibleLearningHost.identity: Nexus generates a per-workspace RSA-2048 OIDC signing identity and a 32-byte random transport key. Private material is encrypted with Electron safeStorage outside the workspace and is never exposed through renderer IPC or written into the plugin store.
crucibleLearningHost.provisioning: The plugin security view installs and enables the bundled Crucible plugin, invokes its secure configuration action, and fails closed unless the plugin reports learning readiness as green.
crucibleLearningHost.verification: Automated tests cover workspace separation, OIDC signature and claims, short token lifetime, secret scoping, installation, configuration persistence, and final readiness. Hosted exact-tip CI remains required after push.
